title: The Wild Veil Again
premise: In the mountain nation of Thornfell, magic survives only in smugglers' bloodlines, and Lena Whitlock has spent her life hiding her gift behind her guild's silence. When the crown's Veilhunt begins burning villages to flush out the gifted, Lena discovers her guildmaster sold the guild's names to buy his own pardon. Fleeing with a hunted cartographer named Ivo, she searches for the Hollow Door, a passage said to lead out of Thornfell—but the Door only opens for those who remember the country as it truly was, and the crown is erasing that memory from every map and mind. In the end, Lena chooses to stay behind at the Door, feeding it her own memories of home so Ivo and the last gifted children can escape, becoming the living archive of a country that no longer exists.
about_author: Theo Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former trail guide who spent six years mapping abandoned passes in eastern Europe before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about borders, memory, and the people who live in the gaps between maps.

chapters.title: Salt on the Pass
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She runs contraband through the Thornfell high roads for the near-dead Smugglers' Guild, hiding a small flare of magic when a rockslide threatens her caravan. The beat is quiet competence shadowed by fear—she saves lives but knows each use of the gift leaves a trace someone might read.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. In the lowland town of Greyford, criers announce the Veilhunt: all gifted persons must register or be taken. A neighbor Lena has known for years denounces a family overnight. The emotional beat is the collapse of the ordinary—the realization that invisibility was always a story she told herself.

chapters.title: What the Guild Knew
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She returns to the guildhall to find it emptied; her guildmaster, Aldous, has traded the membership rolls to the crown in exchange for pardon. His POV interlude shows his rationalizations. The beat is betrayal sharpened into clarity: survival has a price, and he paid with other people.

chapters.title: The Cartographer
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A disgraced royal mapmaker who hid gifted children in false border lines, Ivo is cornered by hunters until Lena, following rumor, pulls him out. Their uneasy alliance forms. The beat is two strangers recognizing the same wound—he erased places to save people; she erased herself.

chapters.title: Roads That No Longer Are
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The pair travel using Ivo's pre-Veil maps toward the Hollow Door, passing villages where names have been struck from signs and elders' memories seem sanded smooth. The beat is mounting dread: the hunt isn't just killing the gifted, it's unmaking the country they belong to.

chapters.title: The Tollhouse
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Captured by a hunter captain who was once a guild runner she trained, Lena bargains with shared memory instead of violence, buying a day's head start—and learning the crown needs a living gifted person to seal the Door forever. The beat is painful mercy toward someone complicit in the hunt.

chapters.title: Children of the Fold
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. They reach a hidden fold where Ivo's rescued children wait, starving and afraid, including a girl whose gift lets her hear memories in stone. Through her, Lena glimpses what the Door demands. The beat is reluctant hope hardening into responsibility—these children are now hers to carry.

chapters.title: The Hollow Door
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. At the Door beneath a glacier, they find it half-sealed, answering only to true remembrance of Thornfell. Hunters close in; Aldous appears among them, begging Lena to surrender. The climax begins: she touches the stone and offers her first memory. The beat is sacrifice chosen with open eyes.

chapters.title: Everything I Kept
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. As hunters breach the cavern, Lena pours memories into the Door—her mother's kitchen, every pass, Aldous himself as he once was—widening it while Ivo drives the children through. Aldous breaks, turning on the hunters. The beat is grief transfigured into an act of preservation.

chapters.title: The Wild Veil
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, then Lena's. Beyond the border, the children grieve a homeland they can no longer picture—but Lena remains on the threshold, the Door's keeper, remembering everything. Ivo plants a seed of wild veil-flowers over the site. The resolution holds both loss and continuity: a country survives inside one woman's keeping.
